keyScheme: first three FEN fields (board, side to move, castling); en passant excluded like book.js; every stored move re-verified legal with ep cleared

featureDefinitions.check: opponent king is attacked after the move
featureDefinitions.queenTrade: a queen is captured, or the queen moves to a square where it can be taken at once
featureDefinitions.centralPawn: pawn moves to d4/e4/d5/e5, or a two-square push onto ranks 4/5 of files c-f
featureDefinitions.develop: knight or bishop leaves the back rank
featureDefinitions.recapture: captures on the square the opponent just landed on (needs the previous ply, so it is counted, not inferred)
featureDefinitions.kingZone: destination inside the 5x5 box around the enemy king
featureDefinitions.hanging: the moved piece can be captured immediately by a piece worth at most as much (and the move gives no check)
featureDefinitions.inBook: the human move is present in Kiwa's opening book entry for this key
featureDefinitions.quiet: not a capture, not castling, not a promotion
featureDefinitions.queenMove: the moved piece is a queen

evalCoverage.note: measured on the EVAL split only; this table was fit on TRAIN only

caveats: Counts come from Lichess blitz/bullet games of mostly amateur players.
A position seen once has count 1: the table is noisy at the tail, which is what the smoothing/backoff in the harness is for.
Feature marginals over all legal moves are computed on the same train positions (denominator = sum of legal move counts).
